html:
Takrur was a kingdom on the middle Senegal River, in what is now northern Senegal, at its height in the 1000s and 1100s. The map shows it from 1000 to 1200.

Its ruler War Jabi, who died in 1041, became a Muslim and imposed Islamic law, making Takrur one of the first West African states to adopt Islam. Takrur then fought alongside the Almoravids in the Sahara. It traded gold, slaves and grain north across the desert and rivalled the Ghana Empire to the east.

In the 1200s Takrur fell under the Mali Empire, though it kept its own rulers. Arab writers later used "Takrur" as a name for all the Muslims of West Africa. The region became Futa Toro, and its people are the Toucouleur, a name that comes from Takrur.
